name: rivet-buck-set
title: Rivet Buck Set
description: A pin/lock control built from hot-driven riveting: a shop head forms under five discrete hammer strikes, then keeps drawing the two sheets together for a moment after its shape stops changing, as the shank cools and shrinks — legible as the joint visibly tightening after the forming flurry ends.
useWhen: a pin/lock/fasten control on a row or card — pinning a message, locking a row, fixing a card in place — that should read as a real mechanical fastening event (forming plus a post-forming clamp) rather than a generic pin-icon rotate or filled/outline swap; the ambient loop runs on its own clock and a press just replays it on demand. Pick copy-field-crimp instead when the fastening event should be a single instantaneous crimp with no separate post-forming clamp phase, or checkbox-domino-run when the surface being toggled is a plain boolean checkbox rather than a pin/lock affordance on a row.
instruction:
A row/card control (flex row: heading + mono description on the left, a square fastener button on the right) whose button renders a hot-driven rivet joint sourced from aircraft-structures solid riveting practice, not a generic pin icon. The button is `aspect-square`, its own size measured via ResizeObserver on itself (not the outer card) so geometry derives from the button's own smaller dimension per the binding rule, and all reference numbers below are authored at a REF=112px panel size then multiplied by `scale = measuredSize/112` so they hold proportionally at other sizes.

The shop head is an SVG path rebuilt every frame from four control radii at fixed heights (base/lower-mid/upper-mid/apex, height fractions [0, 0.35, 0.7, 1] of a 30px*scale head region) mirrored left/right and run through a midpoint-quadratic smoothing pass (for each consecutive pair of silhouette points, `L` to the first midpoint then `Q` through the point to the next midpoint) so the dome reads as forged metal, not a polygon. Baseline (unformed) radius is 5px*scale at every level, a plain proud cylinder. Five discrete hammer strikes land 90ms apart (450ms total forming) with decaying per-strike control-radius increments 3.4/2.1/1.3/0.8/0.5px*scale (~0.62 geometric decay, matching work-hardening reducing each blow's effect); each level's share of a strike's increment is scaled by a per-level weight [1, 0.85, 0.55, 0.15] (base to apex) so growth concentrates toward the base and produces a mushroom/dome silhouette rather than a uniform balloon. Each strike also runs a 40ms shock: for the first 35% of that window the radius overshoots to 1.3x the settling increment (easeOutCubic), then eases back down to exactly 1x by 40ms (easeInOutCubic) — this uses a `computeGrowth(t)` that walks every strike whose start time has passed and sums `weight * delta * (t within that strike's 40ms window ? overshootMultiplier(u) : 1)`, so calling it with any t past 450ms naturally yields the fully-settled sum with no separate branch needed. The five strikes must stay visually discrete (per-strike overshoot-then-settle), never a smooth ramp — collapsing them into one continuous deformation is a reject per the spec's own kill criterion.

Two plain `<div>` sheet panels sandwich the head's base at `headBaseY = 52%` of the button's size: an upper sheet fixed at that line with a fixed thickness, and a lower sheet whose `top` is set every frame to `headBaseY + sheetThickness + currentGap` with its `height` filling to the button's bottom edge — so the lower sheet's top edge is the only thing that visibly moves, reading directly as the sheets drawing together with no change to the head geometry. `currentGap` starts at 6px*scale (bare shank, sheets at rest) and is unaffected during the 450ms forming window (the shape finishing does not by itself move the sheets). From 450ms to 2250ms (the 1800ms post-forming shrink/clamp window, well after visible forming stops), `currentGap` eases (easeOutCubic) down by 2px*scale and the BASE control radius (index 0 only) additionally tightens by up to 1px*scale over the same window — this is the one thing a viewer should be able to follow: the head's silhouette is already finished and static by 450ms, and the joint keeps visibly tightening for another 1.8s after that, which is what separates a hot-driven rivet from a generic squash-and-stop animation. 2250-3850ms holds at full clamp. 3850-4250ms eases (easeInOutCubic) the whole formed state — growth multiplier, gap, base tightening — back to the bare unformed shank and starting gap, then the 4250ms period loops continuously with zero input required. If the post-forming gap narrowing is imperceptible, reject — that is the spec's other explicit kill criterion.

Colour: the head fill is `var(--foreground)` with a `var(--border)` outline and the two sheet panels use `bg-foreground/[0.08]` — pure CSS custom properties, no JS colour math needed since there's no canvas/WebGL here, and a theme flip repaints for free. The one exception is a second, invisible-until-flashed `<path>` sharing the exact same `d` as the head, stroked in `var(--foreground)` with `stroke-opacity` driven straight off each strike's shock envelope (0 baseline, animated up during each 40ms shock window, back to 0 by its end) — a luminance-only 'catching the light' glint at the rim on each strike, never a colour change and never `--ns-accent`. Its peak opacity is capped at 0.85 in dark theme and 0.4 in light theme (checked directly against a light background, where less headroom is available before a flash reads as blown-out); the dark/light branch comes from one cheap `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` read of `--background`'s relative luminance at mount, re-derived on a `MutationObserver` watching `documentElement`'s class flip, never per-frame.

Interaction: `pointerdown` on the button, or `Enter`/`Space` via a `keydown` listener (native `<button>` handles focus/keyboard reachability), resets the cycle-start timestamp to `performance.now()` — since the ambient loop already runs on its own unconditional clock, a press simply replays the same 4.25s sequence from t=0 rather than a separate state machine, so `autoplay.mode` stays `"none"` (the motion never depends on the synthetic-input driver to begin with). The 90ms strike cadence and 40ms shock stay identical whether the cycle was started by the ambient loop or a press — collapsing the interaction-triggered version into a single smooth deformation would lose the mechanic the same way a passive ambient loop would.

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` freezes on `STATIC_T = 2650ms` (450ms forming + 1800ms clamp + 400ms into the 1600ms hold), named `STATIC_PHASE = "clamped"` and exposed as `data-reduced-motion-freeze` on the root — shop head fully formed, sheets fully drawn together at minimum gap, the only frame showing the completed joint (the bare-shank frame shows nothing formed yet). Standard cleanup: ResizeObserver on the button, IntersectionObserver (threshold default) pausing the rAF loop off-screen, `visibilitychange` pausing when the tab is hidden, MutationObserver for theme, all disconnected and the rAF cancelled on unmount. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG only, no canvas.
